payload.rationale: This document is a sprint retro that closely mirrors the existing Sprint 4 retro (2026-03-22) but is dated 2026-08-10 with only Tanya as participant. I expanded the prior retro sample so passes can relate this new retro to the existing one; the anti-Slack positioning narrative and its child positions (product category, anti-pattern, thesis proven) to give context for what the async decision widget is and why it matters; the Zephyr integration unlock position and the rate-limit resolution observation so passes can bind the 'key unlock' claim rather than minting a duplicate; the Tina velocity observation (same 23-point claim, different reporter and date) so passes can extend or note the divergence; and the metric-anchor style observation since the document uses the exact same quantified phrasing. I deliberately did not expand pricing or target-market positions since the document mentions neither.

The map and index never vary with your focus; your per-call material is at the end.

^-marked entries are compressed stubs carrying child addresses. Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). Decide from the map; expand to ground.

positions.frame: what does completing the widget deliverable alongside a peak velocity figure establish about this sprint's execution?
positions.why: Both expressions are flat, past-tense, realis reports of completed sprint outcomes (shipping the widget, hitting 23 points) delivered in the same matter-of-fact/technical register with an informational stance — read together they assert the sprint's execution as an accomplished, measurable fact rather than an aspiration or plan.

positions.name: SprintVelocityAttributedToZephyr
positions.frame: what accounts for this sprint's velocity spike?
positions.why: The velocity figure and the Zephyr-as-'key unlock' claim are causally linked in the same breath — the metric is offered as the effect and the integration as its named cause, both delivered with the same confident, unhedged claim-level conviction and competence-framed value appeal; the pairing reads as a single causal attribution rather than two separate facts.

placements.why: Shipping the async decision widget and hitting a peak 23-point velocity are reported together as the sprint's proof-in-execution of the anti-Slack thesis — a persistent, structured decision artifact actually shipped and measured, not just positioned. Both are flat, past-tense, realis facts that evidence the positioning claim being realized rather than a standalone theme of their own.

The velocity spike is causally tied in the same breath to the Zephyr integration, which embeds decision capture directly in Slack/Teams/Discord threads without separate plugins — the technical mechanism that makes 'zero extra steps' capture-at-consensus possible. The metric and the named unlock together evidence this narrative's core claim rather than standing as an isolated fact.
